title: About
body:
Scott Hunt

Scott Hunt is an award-winning photographer and educator who has spent over three decades shaping the next generation of visual artists while maintaining an active career as a working photographer. He holds an M.F.A. in Photography and Art History from Texas A&M University-Commerce and a B.S. in Photography from East Texas State University, beginning his teaching career there as a Graduate Assistant and Ad-Interim Assistant Professor before building the program that would define his legacy.

Since 1998, Hunt has served as Photography Instructor at St. Mark’s School of Texas, where he built the department’s curriculum from the ground up and guided it through the transition to digital media. In recognition of his sustained excellence in the classroom, he was named to the Arnold E. Holtberg Master Teaching Chair (2014–2025) — one of only sixteen endowed teaching positions at the school. Since 2025, Hunt has served as the Tony Vintcent Fine Arts Department Chair. Under his direction, the St. Mark’s Photography Program has been named “Top Program” by the Association of Texas Photography Instructors sixteen times since 2007, and his students have earned fourteen “Winners with Distinction” and twenty-five “Winners” honors in the National Young Arts Competition, including three U.S. Presidential Scholars in the Arts since 2004 — the nation’s highest honor for a graduating high school artist.

Beyond the classroom, Hunt has directed St. Mark’s Student Travel Programs since 2016, building a global education initiative that has taken students to Thailand, Italy, Bhutan, Peru, Morocco, Cambodia, Argentina, Laos, France, Czech Republic, Turkey and Spain. Altogether, Hunt’s work has taken him to nearly 30 countries. In 2026, Hunt co-chaired the Independent School Association of the Southwest’s Fine Arts Festival Steering Committee — directing a three-day festival drawing over 3,000 student artists from six states. His teaching experience also extends to the collegiate level, with adjunct and faculty appointments at Dallas College and Texas A&M University-Commerce.

As the owner of Scott Hunt Photography since 1993, Hunt has produced commercial and editorial work for clients including Electronic Data Systems, Electronic Arts, J.C. Penney, Gulf Oil, PaineWebber, and The Dallas Morning News. His photographs have appeared in more than thirty publications across North America, Europe, and Africa, including Life, Texas Monthly, D Magazine, Communication Arts, Graphis, HOW, and American Way. His exhibition history spans solo and group shows from the Philbrook Museum of Art and Oklahoma Museum of Art early in his career to the Texas Photographic Society’s 39th Members Only Show in 2026, with notable solo and faculty exhibitions including The Space Between (2004) and Bhutan: Happiness Discovered (2007).

Hunt’s artistic and educational contributions have been widely recognized, including the White House Commission on Presidential Scholars’ Distinguished Teacher Award (2019, 2020, 2024), the Ralph B. Rogers Alumni Award from St. Mark’s School of Texas (2023), the John H. Murrell Excellence in Teaching Award (2003), the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards Outstanding Teacher honor (2013, 2014, 2025), the Houston Art Directors Club Gold Medal (1999), a Gold Medal from the Council for the Advancement and Support of Education (2003), a Society of Publication Designers Merit Award (1999), and recognition as a runner-up for the Alfred Eisenstaedt Award for Magazine Photography (1999). He is a member of the Association for Experiential Education, the Association of Texas Photography Instructors, the Texas Photographic Society, and the Society for Photographic Education.
